parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskService is an application-layer use-case service, and its responsibilities fit that role. Each public method (createUser, createProject, createTask, listTasks, markDone) handles one use case. It checks input, confirms that referenced entities exist through the injected TaskRepository port, generates IDs and hands work to the repository. The file contains no persistence code: no SQL, no file or storage access, and no repository implementation. It also has no transport or framework code such as HTTP request/response handling, status codes or routing. Errors are raised as domain-level DomainError codes, not HTTP codes. One borderline point: markDone holds a state-transition invariant itself ("already done" → CONFLICT, then sets task.status = "done"), and createTask checks status values against taskStatuses. A richer design would move these onto the domain entity. Still, this is application logic driving the domain, not a responsibility from a different kind of layer as the rubric means it (for example persistence or transport code in domain, or business rules in infrastructure). So it is a design-quality point, not a layer-role violation.
